title: How the fraud model learns what mistakes cost
subtitle: Transactions pass data gates and leak-free features, then XGBoost and a cost sweep decide which purchases get flagged.

nodes.label: Raw transactions
nodes.detail: Loads the raw purchase records (user, device, IP, browser, source, value, signup and purchase times) and saves them as snappy-compressed Parquet.
nodes.tradeoff: Every row carries both signup and purchase times, which the checks and features downstream depend on.

nodes.label: Data gates
nodes.detail: Checks rows against a JSON schema, that signup comes before purchase, that under 5% of values are missing, and that fraud makes up 5% to 15%.
nodes.tradeoff: The quality gate exits with an error code, so an automated run stops before training on bad data.

nodes.label: Feature builder
nodes.detail: Builds account age, time of day, purchase counts per device and IP over 1-hour and 24-hour windows, amount z-scores, and target-encoded browser and source.
nodes.tradeoff: Windows count only earlier transactions, and target encoding uses K-fold, so the label can't leak into the features.

nodes.label: Cross-validation
nodes.detail: Each model type runs 5-fold stratified cross-validation, recording AUC, precision, recall, F1 and total cost for every fold.
nodes.tradeoff: A 20% test set, split with the fraud ratio kept, is held back for the final numbers.

nodes.label: XGBoost model
nodes.detail: XGBoost learns a fraud probability with scale_pos_weight set to the cost ratio, 100 / 5 = 20. Logistic regression and LightGBM share the same interface.
nodes.tradeoff: Weighting by cost favours recall: the committed results show XGBoost at 0.70 recall and 0.22 precision on the test set.

nodes.label: Cost threshold
nodes.detail: Tries 101 thresholds from 0 to 1 and keeps the cheapest: false alarms times $5 plus missed fraud times $100.
nodes.tradeoff: In the committed results it settled at 0.46 for XGBoost and 0.52 for logistic regression, not the default 0.5.

nodes.label: Performance gate
nodes.detail: Re-scores the saved model on the test set and checks AUC of at least 0.75, precision 0.60, recall 0.70 and F1 0.60.
nodes.tradeoff: Any failed check exits with code 1, so a CI job can refuse to ship the model.

nodes.label: MLflow registry
nodes.detail: Helpers log parameters, cost settings, metrics and plots, register models, and promote the best model by AUC to Production.
nodes.tradeoff: The MLflow server runs in Docker from the v2.5.0 image, storing runs and artifacts on local disk.

flow.text: Loads the raw purchase records and saves them as Parquet.
Checks schema, time order, missing values and fraud ratio; stops if any fail.
Counts each device's and IP's purchases in the hour and day before.
Runs 5-fold cross-validation to see how stable each model is.
Fits XGBoost with missed fraud weighted 20 times a false alarm.
Sweeps 101 cut-offs and keeps the cheapest, 0.46 in the committed run.
Fails the build if AUC, precision, recall or F1 fall short.
Logs the run and promotes the best model by AUC.

takeaways.text: The flag threshold minimises $5 per false alarm plus $100 per missed fraud, instead of defaulting to 0.5.
Velocity windows count only earlier transactions, so features never see the future they are meant to predict.
Data and model gates exit with code 1, letting CI block bad data or a weak model.
